claim: RseP belongs to the S2P family of intramembrane-cleaving proteases.
source: Escherichia coli RseP belongs to S2P zinc metalloproteinase family of I-CLiPs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction and is established knowledge about RseP classification.

claim: RseP plays a key role in regulating the σE extracytoplasmic stress response.
source: It plays a key role in regulating the σE extracytoplasmic stress response (Hizukuri et al., 2013; Kroos and Akiyama, 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: RseP catalyzes site-2 cleavage of RseA after DegS-mediated site-1 cleavage.
source: The first cleavage catalysed by DegS (site-1 cleavage) on the periplasmic side triggers the intramembrane cleavage by RseP (site-2 cleavage) (Alba et al., 2002; Kanehara et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: RseP acts in the proteolytic removal of remnant signal peptides from the membrane.
source: Recent studies suggest that in addition to being involved in RseA cleavage, RseP acts in the proteolytic removal of remnant signal peptides from the membrane (Saito et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: RseP spans the membrane 4 times with both termini facing the periplasm.
source: RseP spans the membrane 4 times, with both the termini facing the periplasm.
evidence: This is a structural description of RseP based on established knowledge.

claim: RseP contains tandem PDZ domains (PDZ-N and PDZ-C) in its central periplasmic region.
source: Its central periplasmic region contains tandem PDZ domains (PDZ-N and PDZ-C; Figure 1A) (Kanehara et al., 2001; Kinch et al., 2006; Inaba et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: S2P family proteases share a conserved core domain containing 3 transmembrane segments.
source: The S2P family proteases share a conserved core domain containing 3 TMs. In RseP, these correspond to TM1–TM3 (Figure 1A,B) (Kinch et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation and reference to figures.

claim: The first and third transmembrane segments of RseP contain HExxH and LDG active site motifs, respectively.
source: The first and the third TM contain HExxH and LDG active site motifs, respectively.
evidence: This is a structural description of RseP's active site.

claim: TM3 of RseP plays a critical role in binding of a substrate TM.
source: Disulfide crosslinking and co-immunoprecipitation experiments suggest that TM3 plays a critical role in binding of a substrate TM (Koide et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous experimental work.

claim: Helix destabilisation of substrate TMs promotes their binding to and cleavage by RseP.
source: Helix destabilisation of substrate TMs promotes their binding to and cleavage by RseP (Akiyama et al., 2004; Koide et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: RseP-catalysed site-2 cleavage of RseA depends on site-1 cleavage.
source: RseP-catalysed site-2 cleavage of RseA depends on site-1 cleavage (Alba et al., 2002; Kanehara et al., 2002)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Site-1 cleavage is induced by stress signals.
source: site-1 cleavage is induced by stress signals (Walsh et al., 2003; Kulp and Kuehn, 2011; Lima et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: RseP PDZ domains are involved in the site-1 cleavage-dependence of the site-2 cleavage.
source: Previous studies suggest that RseP PDZ domains are involved in the site-1 cleavage-dependence of the site-2 cleavage by RseP (Kanehara et al., 2003; Bohn et al., 2004; Grigorova et al., 2004; Inaba et al., 2008; Hizukuri and Akiyama, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The crystal structure of mjS2P from Methanocaldococcus jannaschii has been reported.
source: Although the crystal structure of an S2P homolog (mjS2P) from Methanocaldococcus jannaschii (Feng et al., 2007) has been reported
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claim: mjS2P does not have a PDZ domain.
source: it does not have a PDZ domain
evidence: This is a structural observation about mjS2P.

claim: The crystal structure of the PDZ tandem of an Aquifex aeolicus RseP homolog has been reported.
source: We recently reported the crystal structure of the PDZ tandem of an Aquifex aeolicus RseP homolog.
evidence: This is a statement about the authors' previous work.

claim: The 2 PDZ domains create a single pocket-like structure that covers the core membrane domain on the membrane surface.
source: The structure suggests that the 2 PDZ domains create a single pocket-like structure that covers the core membrane domain on the membrane surface (Hizukuri et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous structural work.

claim: The PDZ tandem acts as a size-exclusion filter to allow only the periplasmically truncated form of RseA to enter the recessed active site.
source: Structural models and biochemical and genetic results suggest that the PDZ tandem acts as a size-exclusion filter to allow only the periplasmically truncated form of RseA to enter the recessed active site in the membrane domain of RseP (Kroos and Akiyama, 2013; Hizukuri et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: mjS2P contains a region that is looped into the membrane domain from the cytoplasmic side.
source: The structure of mjS2P indicates that it contains a region, located close to the active site, that is looped into the membrane domain from the cytoplasmic side (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of mjS2P crystal structure.

claim: The membrane-reentrant loop is in an extended or β-strand conformation.
source: This membrane-reentrant loop is unique because it is in an extended or β-strand conformation
evidence: This is based on structural analysis.

claim: The membrane-reentrant loop has been named MRE β-loop.
source: Therefore, we have named this region membrane-reentrant β-loop (MRE β-loop).
evidence: This is a nomenclature decision by the authors.

claim: The MRE β-loop is conserved in proteins belonging to groups I and III of S2P subfamilies.
source: The MRE β-loop is conserved in proteins belonging to groups I and III of S2P subfamilies, including RseP (group I), Bacillus subtilis SpoIVFB (group III) and mjS2P (group III; Figure 1D) (Ha, 2009; Kroos and Akiyama, 2013; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis and citations.

claim: The MRE β-loop of SpoIVFB can be crosslinked with a substrate through disulfide bonds.
source: A recent study showed that the MRE β-loop of SpoIVFB can be crosslinked with a substrate through disulfide bonds, suggesting its possible involvement in substrate interaction (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Deletion of the MRE β-loop (Δloop mutant) did not cause global structural changes in RseP.
source: Accumulation level of the Δloop mutant of RseP-HM (RseP with a C-terminal His-Myc bipartite tag) was comparable to that of wild-type RseP-HM (Figure 2), suggesting that the Δloop mutation did not cause global structural changes in RseP.
evidence: This is inferred from comparable protein accumulation levels shown in Figure 2.

claim: The Δloop mutant did not exhibit complementation activity against a ΔrseP mutation.
source: The Δloop mutant did not exhibit complementation activity against a ΔrseP mutation (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown by experimental data in Figure 2A.

claim: The Δloop mutant was proteolytically inactive against HA-MBP-RseA148 and HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148.
source: Co-expression of the substrates with the Δloop mutant did not convert them from FL to CL, indicating that the mutant was proteolytically inactive.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing no substrate cleavage.

claim: HA-MBP-YqfG was cleaved by wild-type RseP-HM but not by RseP-HM E23Q mutant.
source: The protein was converted to a slightly smaller fragment upon co-expression with wild-type RseP-HM but not with RseP-HM E23Q mutant, indicating that HA-MBP-YqfG was cleaved by RseP presumably within its TM.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing substrate cleavage.

claim: The Δloop mutant did not cleave HA-MBP-YqfG.
source: As expected, the Δloop mutant did not cleave HA-MBP-YqfG.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: HA-MBP-YoaJ did not undergo any cleavage by RseP.
source: In contrast, HA-MBP-YoaJ did not undergo any cleavage (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is shown by experimental data in Figure 2F.

claim: Most HA-MBP-YoaJ was integrally associated with the membrane.
source: Cell fractionation and alkali extraction showed that most HA-MBP-YoaJ was integrally associated with the membrane (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is shown by cell fractionation experiments.

claim: RseP selectively cleaves type II membrane proteins, even those with a small periplasmic domain.
source: These results show that the MRE β-loop plays a critical role in the proteolytic function of RseP and that RseP selectively cleaves type II membrane proteins, even those with a small periplasmic domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential cleavage of YqfG (cleaved) and YoaJ (not cleaved).

claim: All single Cys mutants of RseP, except G68C, supported normal cell growth and cleaved HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148.
source: Complementation and model substrate cleavage assays showed that all the single Cys mutants, except G68C supported normal cell growth and cleaved HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from complementation and cleavage assays.

claim: The G68C mutant cleaved the model substrate with slightly lower but significant efficiency.
source: Although the G68C mutant was inactive in complementation, it cleaved the model substrate with a slightly lower but significant efficiency.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: No residue in the MRE β-loop is specifically required for the proteolytic function of RseP.
source: These results indicate that no residue in the MRE β-loop is specifically required for the proteolytic function of RseP.
evidence: This is inferred from the Cys-scanning mutagenesis results.

claim: Pro substitution at positions 67, 68, 69 and 70 abolished complementation.
source: In contrast to the results for Cys mutants, Pro substitution at positions 67, 68, 69 and 70, which are thought to be located in the distal part (Leu-66 to Glu-75) of the MRE β-loop, abolished complementation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from complementation assays.

claim: The G68P mutant efficiently cleaved HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 but was almost completely defective in cleaving HA-MBP-RseA148.
source: Interestingly, the G68P mutant, which was almost completely defective in cleaving HA-MBP-RseA148, efficiently cleaved HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing differential substrate cleavage.

claim: Pro mutations in the MRE β-loop exerted more profound effects on the cleavage of HA-MBP-YqfG than on the cleavage of the other 2 model substrates.
source: Pro mutations in the MRE β-loop exerted more profound effects on the cleavage of HA-MBP-YqfG than on the cleavage of the other 2 model substrates.
evidence: This is based on experimental data comparing cleavage of different substrates.

claim: The initial rates of HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 and HA-MBP-YqfG cleavage by RseP-HM were slightly lower than that of HA-MBP-RseA148 cleavage.
source: We found that the initial rates of HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 and HA-MBP-YqfG cleavage by co-expressed RseP-HM were slightly lower than that of HA-MBP-RseA148 cleavage (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is based on pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: The G68P mutant significantly cleaved HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 during the 15 min chase period.
source: During the 15 min chase period, the G68P mutant significantly cleaved HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 (Figure 2H)
evidence: This is based on pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: The K71P mutant efficiently cleaved HA-MBP-RseA148 and HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 but only slightly cleaved HA-MBP-YqfG.
source: while the K71P mutant efficiently cleaved HA-MBP-RseA148 and HA-MBP-RseA(LY1)148 but only slightly cleaved HA-MBP-YqfG, which was consistent with immunoblotting results (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is based on pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: The MRE β-loop mutations resulted in the differential cleavage of different model substrates.
source: Thus, the intrinsic susceptibility of each model substrate to wild-type RseP was not correlated with its susceptibility to MRE β-loop mutants, indicating that the MRE β-loop mutations resulted in the differential cleavage of different model substrates.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of mutations on different substrates.

claim: Wild-type RseP-HM was co-immunoprecipitated with HA-MBP-RseA and vice versa.
source: Consistent with the previous results, wild-type RseP-HM was co-immunoprecipitated with HA-MBP-RseA and HA-MBP-RseA was co-immunoprecipitated with RseP-HM
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: No co-immunoprecipitation was observed with RseP-HM having an N389L mutation.
source: but no co-immunoprecipitation was observed with RseP-HM having an N389L mutation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: Deletion of the MRE β-loop almost completely abolished co-immunoprecipitation.
source: Deletion of the MRE β-loop almost completely abolished co-immunoprecipitation, suggesting its importance in RseP–substrate interaction (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: All the MRE β-loop Pro mutants, except D74P, significantly decreased co-immunoprecipitation efficiency.
source: We found that all the MRE β-loop Pro mutants, except D74P located in the C-terminus of the loop, significantly decreased co-immunoprecipitation efficiency, indicating that the Pro mutations compromised the interaction between RseP-HM and model substrates (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: The MRE β-loop is required for stable substrate binding by RseP.
source: The result that absence of or mutations in the MRE β-loop interfered with RseP–substrate interaction suggests that the MRE β-loop is required for stable substrate binding by RseP.
evidence: This is inferred from co-immunoprecipitation results.

claim: RseP-HM was co-immunoprecipitated with HA-MBP-YoaJ in an MRE β-loop-dependent manner.
source: Anti-HA co-immunoprecipitation showed that RseP-HM was pulled down with HA-MBP-YoaJ in an MRE β-loop-dependent manner
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: YoaJ can interact with RseP although it is not cleaved by RseP.
source: indicating that YoaJ can interact with RseP although it is not cleaved by RseP
evidence: This is inferred from co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Overexpression of HA-MBP-YoaJ little affected the cleavage of co-expressed HA-RseA148 by RseP.
source: However, overexpression of HA-MBP-YoaJ little affected the cleavage of co-expressed HA-RseA148 by RseP.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: pBPA-containing RseP-HM proteins decreased the accumulation of RseA148, indicating their functionality.
source: Expression of pBPA-containing RseP-HM proteins decreased the accumulation of RseA148, indicating the functionality of these proteins, although some exhibited lower proteolytic activity against RseA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing substrate cleavage.

claim: UV irradiation produced bands of approximately 71 kDa when pBPA was incorporated at position 69, 71 or 74.
source: Anti-RseA immunoblotting showed UV irradiation produced bands of approximately 71 kDa (XL) when pBPA was incorporated at position 69, 71 or 74, suggesting that these bands represented photo-crosslinked products between RseP-HM and RseA (Figure 4A, upper panels).
evidence: This is based on photo-crosslinking experimental data.

claim: The 71 kDa band represented an RseP–RseA crosslinked product.
source: These results further support the notion that the 71 kDa band was the RseP–RseA crosslinked product.
evidence: This is based on immunoprecipitation experiments confirming the crosslinked product.

claim: The N389L mutation considerably decreased RseA crosslinking at the 3 positions.
source: The N389L mutation that destabilised the RseP–substrate interaction considerably decreased RseA crosslinking at the 3 positions (Figure 4B), suggesting that the photo-crosslinking reflected the functional interaction between RseP and RseA.
evidence: This is based on photo-crosslinking experimental data.

claim: RseP(Y69pBPA)-HM generated a significantly lower amount of the crosslinked product in the ΔdegS strain than in the degS+ strain.
source: RseP(Y69pBPA)-HM generated a significantly lower amount of the crosslinked product in the ΔdegS strain than in the degS+ strain, indicating that the MRE β-loop mainly interacts with the DegS-cleaved form of RseA.
evidence: This is based on photo-crosslinking experimental data comparing degS+ and ΔdegS strains.

claim: The oxidant treatment generated a ∼75 kDa band that reacted with both anti-HA and anti-Myc antibodies when Y69C and K71C variants but not Cys-less and V70C variants of RseP-HM were co-expressed with HA-RseA(A108C/C109A)140.
source: The oxidant treatment generated a ∼75 kDa band that reacted with both anti-HA and anti-Myc antibodies when Y69C and K71C variants but not Cys-less and V70C variants of RseP-HM were co-expressed with HA-RseA(A108C/C109A)140 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on disulfide crosslinking experimental data.

claim: The crosslinked band disappeared when the samples were treated with 2-mercaptoethanol before SDS-PAGE.
source: This band disappeared when the samples were treated with 2-mercaptoethanol before SDS-PAGE (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing disulfide bond cleavage.

claim: The MRE β-loop was near the RseP cleavage site.
source: These results were consistent with those of photo-crosslinking experiments because pBPA at positions 69 and 71 but not at position 70 was crosslinked with RseA, indicating that the MRE β-loop was near the RseP cleavage site.
evidence: This is inferred from crosslinking data.

claim: The MRE β-loop can directly bind to substrate TMs.
source: Together, our results strongly suggest that the MRE β-loop can directly bind to substrate TMs.
evidence: This is inferred from crosslinking and co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Wild-type RseP-HM cleaved all the HA-MBP-YqfG mutants almost as efficiently as it cleaved the original HA-MBP-YqfG.
source: Wild-type RseP-HM cleaved all the HA-MBP-YqfG mutants almost as efficiently as it cleaved the original HA-MBP-YqfG (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: L11P and L12P mutations but not other mutations appreciably increased the cleavage by RseP(G67P)-HM.
source: L11P and L12P mutations but not other mutations appreciably increased the cleavage by RseP(G67P)-HM (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing suppression of MRE β-loop mutations.

claim: Cleavage by RseP(K71P)-HM was markedly improved by mutations other than L12P and L13P.
source: In contrast, cleavage by RseP(K71P)-HM was markedly improved by mutations other than L12P and L13P.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing suppression of MRE β-loop mutations.

claim: RseP(G67P)-HM significantly cleaved HA-MBP-YqfG(L12P) but not HA-MBP-YqfG(I8P).
source: RseP(G67P)-HM significantly cleaved HA-MBP-YqfG(L12P) but not HA-MBP-YqfG(I8P) (Figure 6E)
evidence: This is based on pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: RseP(K71P)-HM efficiently cleaved HA-MBP-YqfG(I8P) but not HA-MBP-YqfG(L12P).
source: and RseP(K71P)-HM efficiently cleaved HA-MBP-YqfG(I8P) but not HA-MBP-YqfG(L12P) (Figure 6F)
evidence: This is based on pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: Replacement of Leu-12 in YqfG by Asn also promoted cleavage by the RseP MRE β-loop Pro mutants.
source: Replacement of Leu-12 in YqfG by Asn, another strong helix-destabilising amino acid, also promoted cleavage by the RseP MRE β-loop Pro mutants.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: Replacement of Leu-12 by a helix-forming Trp residue resulted in no increase in cleavage.
source: However, replacement of the same residue by a helix-forming Trp residue resulted in no increase in cleavage (Figure 6A–C), suggesting that helix destabilisation is important for improving substrate cleavage.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: Helix destabilisation is important for improving substrate cleavage.
source: suggesting that helix destabilisation is important for improving substrate cleavage.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of helix-destabilizing vs. helix-forming mutations.

claim: The I8P or L12P mutation did not promote cleavage by the RseP Δloop variant.
source: The I8P or L12P mutation did not promote cleavage by the RseP Δloop variant, indicating that these mutations did not bypass the RseP MRE β-loop function for substrate cleavage (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: The F21P mutation in LY1 significantly improved the cleavage of this TM by RseP(V70P)-HM.
source: the F21P mutation in LY1 significantly improved the cleavage of this TM by RseP(V70P)-HM that was almost inactive in cleavage of wild type LY1, but the Pro substitution of the neighbouring residue, Phe-20, did not.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: Helix-destabilising mutations in substrate TMs at least partially suppress the defects in substrate cleavage induced by Pro substitutions in the RseP MRE β-loop in an allele-specific manner.
source: The results that helix-destabilising mutations in substrate TMs at least partially suppress the defects in substrate cleavage induced by Pro substitutions in the RseP MRE β-loop in an allele-specific manner suggests a specific interaction between substrate TMs and the RseP MRE β-loop.
evidence: This is inferred from the allele-specific suppression data.

claim: Deletion or Pro substitution in the MRE β-loop impaired substrate cleavage.
source: Deletion or Pro substitution in the MRE β-loop impaired substrate cleavage, indicating its critical role in the proteolytic function of RseP.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing impaired cleavage.

claim: The MRE β-loop was directly involved in substrate binding.
source: Crosslinking and co-immunoprecipitation experiments showed that the MRE β-loop was directly involved in substrate binding.
evidence: This is based on crosslinking and co-immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: Several Pro substitutions differentially affected RseP-catalysed proteolysis of substrates.
source: Several Pro substitutions differentially affected RseP-catalysed proteolysis of substrates.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing differential substrate cleavage.

claim: Helix-destabilising mutations in substrate TMs suppressed the defects caused by mutations in the MRE β-loop in an allele-specific manner.
source: Helix-destabilising mutations in substrate TMs suppressed the defects caused by mutations in the MRE β-loop in an allele-specific manner.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing allele-specific suppression.

claim: The MRE β-loop specifically recognises substrate TMs.
source: These results collectively suggest that the MRE β-loop specifically recognises substrate TMs.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects and allele-specific suppression data.

claim: The proximal part of the MRE β-loop has a short β-strand (Ile72-Leu-Leu) in the reported crystal structure of mjS2P.
source: The proximal part of the MRE β-loop has a short β-strand (Ile72-Leu-Leu) in the reported crystal structure of mjS2P (Feng et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the mjS2P crystal structure.

claim: Val80-Ala-Met in the distal part of the MRE β-loop forms a β-strand.
source: Analysis of the secondary structure with STRIDE (Frishman and Argos, 1995) suggested that Val80-Ala-Met in the distal part forms a β-strand (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is based on secondary structure analysis.

claim: The MRE β-loops of RseP and SpoIVFB also have β-strands in the corresponding regions.
source: Sequence-based prediction suggested that the MRE β-loops of RseP and SpoIVFB also have β-strands in the corresponding regions (Figure 1D), suggesting that the MRE β-loop commonly assumes a β-hairpin-like structure.
evidence: This is based on sequence-based secondary structure prediction.

claim: The MRE β-loop commonly assumes a β-hairpin-like structure.
source: suggesting that the MRE β-loop commonly assumes a β-hairpin-like structure.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and sequence analysis.

claim: A higher-order structure of the MRE β-loop is important for the proteolytic function of RseP.
source: These observations suggest that a higher-order structure of the MRE β-loop is important for the proteolytic function of RseP.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of Cys vs. Pro substitutions.

claim: RseP(G68P)-HM significantly cleaved LY1 but only slightly cleaved RseA TM and YqfG TM.
source: Pulse-chase experiments showed that RseP(G68P)-HM significantly cleaved LY1 but only slightly cleaved RseA TM and YqfG TM.
evidence: This is based on pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: RseP(K71P)-HM efficiently cleaved RseA TM and LY1 but only slightly cleaved YqfG TM.
source: In contrast, RseP(K71P)-HM efficiently cleaved RseA TM and LY1 but only slightly cleaved YqfG TM.
evidence: This is based on pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: The effects of MRE β-loop mutations cannot be simply explained by the intrinsic susceptibility of substrates to RseP.
source: Therefore, the effects of MRE β-loop mutations cannot be simply explained by the intrinsic susceptibility of these substrates to RseP.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of mutations on different substrates.

claim: The MRE β-loop specifically recognises substrate TMs.
source: These results suggest that the MRE β-loop specifically recognises substrate TMs.
evidence: This is inferred from the allele-specific suppression data.

claim: Cys residues at positions 69 and 71 of the MRE β-loop disulfide-bonded with Cys residues on either side of the scissile bond in RseA.
source: Cys residues at these positions disulfide-bonded with Cys residues on either side of the scissile bond in RseA.
evidence: This is based on disulfide crosslinking experimental data.

claim: A Cys residue in place of Val-70 in the MRE β-loop of SpoIVFB formed disulfide bonds with Cys residues at several positions around the cleavage site in Pro-σK.
source: A Cys residue in place of Val-70 in the MRE β-loop of SpoIVFB formed disulfide bonds with Cys residues at several positions around the cleavage site in Pro-σK, suggesting that the MRE β-loop of SpoIVFB directly interacts with Pro-σK.
evidence: This is based on citation to a previous study.

claim: Pro-σK is suggested to be peripherally associated with the membrane.
source: In contrast to RseA, which is a single-spanning membrane protein with type II orientation, Pro-σK is suggested to be peripherally associated with the membrane (Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on citation to a previous study.

claim: Helix-destabilising residues in substrate TMs are not required for the cleavage of Pro-σK by SpoIVFB.
source: In addition, although helix-destabilising residues in substrate TMs are important for their efficient cleavage by RseP, these residues are not required for the cleavage of Pro-σK by SpoIVFB (Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on citation to a previous study.

claim: The role of the MRE β-loop in substrate binding and cleavage might slightly differ between RseP and SpoIVFB.
source: Thus, the role of the MRE β-loop in substrate binding and cleavage might slightly differ between RseP and SpoIVFB.
evidence: This is inferred from differences in substrate properties and requirements.

claim: The N389L mutation in RseP TM3 weakens the RseP-substrate interaction.
source: The N389L mutation in RseP TM3, which was previously shown to weaken the RseP-substrate interaction (Koide et al., 2008)
evidence: This is based on citation to a previous study.

claim: The TM4 of mjS2P can be located in the vicinity of the proteolytic active site and the MRE β-loop.
source: The TM4 (corresponding to RseP TM3) of mjS2P that contains one of the active site residues (corresponding to Asp-402 in RseP TM3) can be located in the vicinity of the proteolytic active site and the MRE β-loop (Feng et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and citation.

claim: Cys introduced at the positions of Pro-397 and Pro-399 in RseP TM3 can form a disulfide bond with Cys at multiple positions of RseA TM.
source: We previously showed that Cys introduced at the positions of Pro-397 and Pro-399 in RseP TM3 can form a disulfide bond with Cys at multiple positions of RseA TM.
evidence: This is based on the authors' previous work.

claim: The region containing residues 397 and 399 might be flexible and act with the MRE β-loop in stable binding of a substrate.
source: The region containing residues 397 and 399 might be flexible and act with the MRE β-loop in stable binding of a substrate.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on structural and experimental observations.

claim: Many zinc metalloproteinases have a β-strand (edge strand) close to their proteolytic active site that binds to substrates in an extended conformation through β-strand addition.
source: Many zinc metalloproteinases have a β-strand (edge strand) close to their proteolytic active site that binds to substrates in an extended conformation through β-strand addition and presents them to catalytic residues (Stocker and Bode, 1995; Langklotz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous studies.

claim: The MRE β-loop stabilises the extended conformation of a substrate by directly binding to it through β-strand addition.
source: Our results suggest that the MRE β-loop stabilises the extended conformation of a substrate by directly binding to it through β-strand addition, thus promoting substrate cleavage in a manner similar to the edge strand (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on experimental results.

claim: Crosslinking at alternate positions in the Tyr69-Val-Lys region supports the idea that this region is in a β-strand conformation during its interaction with a substrate.
source: Crosslinking at alternate positions in the Tyr69-Val-Lys region supports the idea that this region is in a β-strand conformation during its interaction with a substrate.
evidence: This is inferred from crosslinking data.

claim: The loop 3 of GlpG and the MRE β-loop of RseP might have a similar role in stabilising an extended substrate structure and promoting its cleavage.
source: Although the loop 3 of GlpG and the MRE β-loop of RseP differ in that the former is located near the periplasmic surface of the membrane and forms a parallel β-sheet with a substrate whereas the latter is located near the cytoplasmic surface and forms a anti-parallel β-sheet, they might have a similar role in stabilising an extended substrate structure and promoting its cleavage.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on comparison with another protease.

claim: The periplasmic PDZ tandem of RseP acts as a size-exclusion filter to prevent the cleavage of substrates with bulky periplasmic domains.
source: We recently suggested that the periplasmic PDZ tandem of RseP acts as a size-exclusion filter to prevent the cleavage of substrates with bulky periplasmic domains (Figure 7A) (Hizukuri et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the authors' previous work.

claim: RseP did not cleave YoaJ, a type II membrane protein with a very small periplasmic domain.
source: In this study, we observed that RseP did not cleave YoaJ, a type II membrane protein with a very small periplasmic domain, suggesting the presence of additional mechanism(s) for substrate discrimination.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: The MRE β-loop interacts with RseA after site 1 cleavage.
source: In vivo photo-crosslinking experiments suggest that the MRE β-loop interacts with RseA after site 1 cleavage (Figure 7B)
evidence: This is based on photo-crosslinking experimental data.

claim: The MRE β-loop acts as the second checkpoint for membrane proteins that passed the first check by the PDZ filter.
source: and that it acts as the second checkpoint for membrane proteins that passed the first check by the PDZ filter and contributes to their selective proteolysis.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on experimental results.

claim: mjS2P does not have PDZ domains.
source: It should be noted that mjS2P does not have PDZ domains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mjS2P structure.

claim: The MRE β-loop could play a central role in cleaving specific substrates in mjS2P.
source: Thus, the MRE β-loop could play a central role in cleaving specific substrates in this enzyme.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the absence of PDZ domains in mjS2P.

claim: RseP directly interacted with intact RseA in the membrane.
source: Although the MRE β-loop may not interact with intact RseA, our previous chemical crosslinking and co-immunoprecipitation experiments showed that RseP directly interacted with intact RseA in the membrane (Kanehara et al., 2003)
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: RseP has a separate binding site (exosite) for intact RseA.
source: suggesting that RseP has a separate binding site (exosite) for intact RseA.
evidence: This is inferred from the interaction with intact RseA despite PDZ filter exclusion.

claim: The presumed exosite may exist on the external surface of the enzyme.
source: Because the PDZ filter excludes intact RseA from the intramolecular active site, the presumed exosite may exist on the external surface of the enzyme.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the PDZ filter model.

claim: Other families of I-CLiPs such as rhomboid and γ-secretase have also been suggested to have an exosite.
source: Other families of I-CLiPs such as rhomboid and γ-secretase have also been suggested to have an exosite (Kornilova et al., 2005; Strisovsky et al., 2009; Watanabe et al., 2010; Arutyunova et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous studies.
